days.title: IAM Fundamentals
days.summary: Users, groups, roles and policies; identity vs resource policies with the real evaluation order — implicit deny by default, an explicit Allow grants, an explicit deny overrides every Allow, cross-account needs Allows on both sides; the six policy types, permissions boundaries, STS temporary credentials, MFA device kinds, Access Analyzer and key hygiene; monitoring with CloudTrail and credential reports. Summary, main concepts, flashcards, true/false and pop quizzes.

days.title: EC2 Compute Fundamentals
days.summary: What belongs on EC2, the four instance controls, launching and connecting (SSH, RDP, Session Manager), the instance lifecycle and status checks, and where EC2 sits on the compute spectrum; instance-type naming, AMI anatomy, user-data bootstrapping with IMDSv2, placement groups (7-per-AZ spread limit), tenancy and the 2024 public-IPv4 $0.005/hour change; plus VPC and load-balancing groundwork basics.

days.title: AWS Lambda Fundamentals
days.summary: Serverless: functions, the three invocation modes, memory-driven CPU (~1,769 MB per vCPU) and the 15-minute ceiling, request + GB-second billing with the permanent free tier, the hard quotas (memory 128 MB–10,240 MB, 6 MB sync / 1 MB async payloads, 4 KB env vars, 10 GB container images), async retries with on-failure destinations and dead-letter queues, reserved vs provisioned concurrency, runtimes/zip/container packaging, versions and aliases, execution roles vs resource policies, and Lambda vs EC2 on the compute spectrum.

days.title: S3 and Storage
days.summary: The EC2 storage trio (EBS vs EFS vs instance store), S3 object storage with 11-nines durability vs designed availability and strong read-after-write consistency, its seven storage classes with the fine print (30/90/180-day minimums, 128 KB minimum objects, per-GB retrieval fees) plus Intelligent-Tiering, versioning, lifecycle and CRR/SRR replication, Block Public Access, presigned URLs and the SSE options, the EBS deep dive (SSD vs HDD, gp2-vs-gp3 tuning, Multi-Attach, incremental snapshots), plus Storage Gateway, AWS Backup, FSx, EFS operating modes and Elastic Disaster Recovery, with clickable tier and type drills.

days.title: AWS Networking Fundamentals
days.summary: Amazon VPC from first principles: region-scoped isolation and your own CIDR, the three networking zones, subnets and tiers across AZs, route tables and the internet gateway, NAT gateways, stateful security groups (cross-group rule sources) vs stateless NACLs with the ephemeral-ports trap, the five reserved IPs and DHCP option sets, gateway vs interface (PrivateLink) VPC endpoints with per-AZ hourly billing, VPC Flow Logs, the two DNS switches, a hands-on two-tier custom VPC build, the inside-out troubleshooting checklist with VPC Reachability Analyzer, and where VPC peering, Transit Gateway and site-to-site VPN fit — with interactive pick-your-fix drills.

days.title: AWS Database Fundamentals
days.summary: Tables, attributes and tuples, primary and foreign keys; Amazon RDS with its five engines and 12-month free tier plus a hands-on EC2-to-RDS build, read replicas (read-scaling, promotable for DR) vs multi-AZ failover, and point-in-time backups vs manual snapshots; the NoSQL trio (key-value, document, graph) and DynamoDB with partition + sort keys, table classes and capacity modes plus the fine print (400 KB items, 4 KB/1 KB capacity units, Streams, Global Tables, DAX); the RDS-vs-DynamoDB comparison on schema, scaling, locking and cost; Amazon Aurora's cluster storage — six-way replication across three AZs, auto-growth to 128 TiB, writer/reader endpoints — and Serverless v2; migration with AWS DMS and SCT; and the in-memory pair, ElastiCache vs MemoryDB for Redis — with a pick-the-DB service-selection drill.

days.title: Understanding AWS Cost Drivers
days.summary: The five cost drivers — compute, storage, databases, data transfer, networking — and what each one's bill depends on; the pricing trio (free tier shapes, Reserved Instances and Savings Plans vs on-demand, plus Spot); Cost Explorer and Billing dashboards with cost-allocation tags, static thresholds and anomaly-detection alerts; the five provisioning decisions and right-sizing with Trusted Advisor and Compute Optimizer; manual vs auto scaling with spend caps; and the six classic overspending scenarios with their mitigations — with a pick-the-pricing-option drill.
